Files I read: the whole request JSON, in two reads (lines 1-1308 and 1309-1741; fingerprint db1e7e98235ee8c8ebbb0bf2bedc91fc16517030b3048daea6a214a0ff5513b6; files: source/original.txt and workflow/source-coverage.json), works/auto-6294ee8a2094/source/original.txt (56 lines), workflow/source-coverage.json (29 spans), source/REVISION-2026-11-11.md (read because the parent asked; it is not in the request's files list), docs/REVISION-AND-REVIEWS.md, docs/PROMPTS.md and the first 30 lines of responses/script-all-r26.json, for the response format. AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md came in as project instructions. All files were readable.

Images: this is a later script comparison, not a first-reading request, so I opened no images. Nothing in this review is a visual check. Whether the 04-3 label now sits on the tablet card and leaves Dr. Ananya's fingers visible depends on the image; the lettering review must check it.

The change since r26: in 04-3 the label text is still 'RAVI · READY'. Its textColumns are now ['RAVI · ', 'READY'], which join back to exactly 'RAVI · READY'. I searched for the literal string 'RAVI · READY' with the same middle-dot character. It matches original.txt line 34, and the request's column 'RAVI · ' uses the same character. The speaker is still 'label'. In 04-3 the scene, production, props and the other caption 'Dr. Ananya is notified when he's ready.' are unchanged from what r26 describes.

Reading order: I read the source before the script. To make up for that, I then re-read only the lettered text in panel order. Each question comes before its answer: 05-1 before 05-2, and 06-2 before 06-3. Each referent comes before the word that points to it: 'the rest' in 01-3 after the paperwork list in 01-2; 'here' in 02-2 after the laptop in 02-1; 'And our team' in 02-3 continues Ananya's 02-2 across a change of speaker, as in the source; 'his own phone' in 03-4 after Ravi is named in 03-3; 'his slot' in 04-1 after 03-3 to 03-5; 'he's ready' in 04-3 after the nurse names Ravi in 04-2; 'your concerns' in 05-4 after 05-2; 'So' and 'That's the idea' on page 6 after 06-1. The script has no apologies, forgiveness or jokes. No line merges turns from different speakers. The only split is Meera's 01-2 line at the ellipsis: same speaker, nothing in between.

Word for word: I checked every caption, line and label in all 27 panels against original.txt and joined every textColumns array. Each one rebuilds its text exactly, trailing spaces included. Four labels are not in the source: 02-1 'WELBUK PRACTICE for the clinic', 02-3 'WELBUK CARE for clinic staff', 06-2 'WELBUK HEALTH for patients', and the repeated 'WELBUK VISION' in 07-3. source-coverage.json records these four as manga supplements. Every speaker matches the source.

Causality and transitions: the morning rush in 01 motivates the onboarding in 02 (time-change to evening). 03-1 'A later morning' marks the next time change. The three check-in routes in 03-1, 03-2 and 03-3/03-4 end in one queue in 03-5 (A-10, A-11, A-12, in check-in order). 04-1 is a short wait later; the chairs are empty because Raman (A-10) and Priya (A-11) were called before 'NOW · A-12'. 04-2 moves to the vitals corner beside reception (place-change). 04-3 cuts to the consultation room. In 05-1 Ravi enters that same room, and the tablet has been put away. 06-1 returns to reception and 06-4 is the departure. 07-1 is a hypothetical train ride ('may'), 07-2 and 07-3 are the vignette vision, and 07-4 returns to the present. Every one of these transitions is recorded with a kind and a bridge.

- Walking stick: raman.right in 03-1 and 03-5.
- Priya's phone: priya.left in 03-2 and 03-5.
- Ravi's phone: right hand in 03-3, both hands in 03-4 (heldBy left), right hand in 03-5, tucked into his pocket in 04-1, in his pocket in 04-2 and on page 5, taken out again into his right hand in 06-1, both hands in 06-2, then his left hand in 06-3, 06-4 and 07-1.

- Desk phone, registers and pen: consistent on page 1.

Costumes: every panel matches its section's costumes. Ananya wears the teal kurta, white coat and stethoscope, never used, in every scene she appears in. Ravi's watch is on his left wrist in 03-4, 04-2 and 06-2. The nurse wears lavender scrubs. Raman and Priya match the reception section. The vision costumes appear only in 07-2 and 07-3, and 07-4 returns to the present-day costumes.

Minor notes, not blocking: 'pen' (01-2) and 'shoulder-bag' are used as prop ids but are not listed in their sections' objects; the bag is described in Ravi's cast entry. In 06-2, Ravi's left hand is on the phone's 'lower right corner' and his right hand on its 'left edge', and the script does not say whether these sides are seen from the reader or from Ravi. The artwork review can check this against the image. Neither point changes dialogue or causality.

What the script alone cannot settle: where the labels sit over the TV (03-5, 04-1) and the tablet (04-3), including the new 04-3 position over the tablet card and whether Ananya's fingers stay visible; balloon order; tails; face and anchor coordinates; and whether the art matches these records. These belong to the artwork, storyboard and lettering reviews. readingReview belongs to those stages, not to this script review.

panels.observation: Caption 'A busy day at Dr. Ananya's clinic.' is verbatim (source line 14). Its columns join exactly. It introduces Ananya by name before she speaks in 01-3.

Meera's source line (line 15) is split at the ellipsis into two same-speaker balloons: 'Appointments, patient details, follow-ups...' and 'I wish everything were easier to manage!'. Both are verbatim and their columns join exactly. No other speaker comes between them. The list sets up 'the rest' in 01-3.

Ananya's 'Our time belongs with patients. Let's make the rest simpler.' is verbatim (line 16) and its columns join exactly. 'the rest' points back to Meera's paperwork list in 01-2. The decision causes the onboarding on page 2.

Caption 'The clinic begins its Welbuk onboarding.' is verbatim (line 19). The label 'WELBUK PRACTICE for the clinic' is a supplement recorded in coverage and names the laptop product in the source panel. Both join exactly. It is a time-change from page 1.
Ananya's 'We can organise our clinic workflow here.' is verbatim (line 20) and joins exactly. 'here' points to the setup laptop shown in 02-1.

Meera's 'And our team can use tools suited to each staff role.' is verbatim (line 21). The label 'WELBUK CARE for clinic staff' is a recorded supplement. Both join exactly. 'And' continues Ananya's 02-2 line across a change of speaker, exactly as in the source.
Ananya's 'One team. Better coordination.' is verbatim (line 22) and joins exactly. The speaker matches the source, and it sums up 02-2 and 02-3.

Caption 'A later morning: patients can always check in at the front desk.' is verbatim from the revised source (line 25) and joins exactly. It introduces 'check in' before 03-2 and gives the time change after the evening onboarding. The speaker is narration.
Caption 'Some check in ahead on the Welbuk Health app.' is verbatim (line 26) and joins exactly. 'Some' contrasts with 'patients can always...' in 03-1.
Caption 'Ravi scans the QR code at the door.' is verbatim (line 27) and joins exactly. It names Ravi, which later 'his' references need.
Caption 'A short form on his own phone, shared with consent.' is verbatim (line 28) and joins exactly. 'his' points back to Ravi in 03-3.

Caption 'Every check-in gets a slot on the screen.' and label 'A-10 · A-11 · A-12' are verbatim (line 29), with the same middle dot. Both join exactly. Slot order follows check-in order: Raman, Priya, Ravi.

Caption 'Soon, his slot comes up.' and label 'NOW · A-12' are verbatim (line 32) and join exactly. 'his' points to Ravi. A-12 is the third slot, as listed in 03-5. The empty chairs explain why A-10 and A-11 are gone.

Caption 'A quick vitals check first.' and the nurse's 'Hi, Ravi! Just relax your arm for me.' are verbatim (line 33) and join exactly. The speaker is the nurse. The line names Ravi, which sets up 'he's' in 04-3. Per the revision log, the line was reworded so it no longer repeats the caption.

Caption 'Dr. Ananya is notified when he's ready.' ('Dr. Ananya is ' + 'notified when ' + 'he's ready.') and label 'RAVI · READY' are verbatim (line 34). The label's columns are now 'RAVI · ' + 'READY', and they join back to exactly 'RAVI · READY'; a literal search with the same middle dot matches the source. The text is unchanged from r26; only the column split and its position changed, and the position is an image check. 'he's' points to Ravi, named in 04-2.
Ananya's 'Hello, Ravi. Tell me what brings you in.' is verbatim (line 37) and joins exactly. It is the question that 05-2 answers. The transition records that Ravi enters the room shown in 04-3.
Ravi's 'I've been feeling tired lately.' is verbatim (line 38) and joins exactly. It answers 05-1 directly. No diagnosis is added.
Caption 'Technology supports the workflow. The conversation stays human.' is verbatim (line 39) and joins exactly. It is a silent listening reaction to 05-2.
Ananya's 'We'll go through your concerns and decide the right next steps together.' is verbatim (line 40) and joins exactly. 'your concerns' points to 05-2. No treatment advice is given.

Meera's 'Welbuk Health is designed to help patients stay connected with their care.' is verbatim (line 43) and joins exactly. It introduces the app that 06-2 asks about. The speaker matches the source.

Ravi's 'So I can keep useful information in one place?' is verbatim (line 44). The label 'WELBUK HEALTH for patients' is a recorded supplement. Both join exactly. 'So' follows from Meera's 06-1 line, and the question comes before Meera's answer in 06-3.

Caption 'Tomorrow, care may take us beyond our hometown.' is verbatim (line 49) and joins exactly. The conditional 'may' keeps the scene hypothetical. It is a time-change to the train.

Label 'WELBUK VISION' (required by the source) and caption 'The vision: trusted connections between clinics, specialists, and patients across locations.' are verbatim (line 50) and join exactly. It is framed as vision, not a launched feature.

Caption 'One connected ecosystem for care and family wellness.' is verbatim (line 51) and joins exactly. The repeated 'WELBUK VISION' label is a recorded supplement that keeps the family scene marked as vision.

Label 'Welbuk Practice • Welbuk Care • Welbuk Health' and caption 'Welbuk — Building a connected healthcare ecosystem.' are verbatim (line 52), including the bullets and the em dash. Both join exactly. The three products pay off the labels in 02-1, 02-3 and 06-2. It returns to the present.
